- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or shows strong bearish signals, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model shows persistent underestimation of mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to reflect medium-term consolidation.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1, 0, 1, 0), model tends to lag by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- In 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.5–1.0), add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days to account for sentiment-driven corrections.
